summary: @onereach/orest-cli preinstall downloads Bun runtime and executes obfuscated bundled payload
details: The package's preinstall hook (`node setup.mjs`) downloads the Bun runtime from the oven-sh/bun GitHub releases, marks it executable, and invokes it against `math_init.js` — a 727KB single-line Bun-CJS bundle shipped in the tarball that carries obfuscator.io fingerprints (rotated string-array decoder `WV8StW`/`n7gIxM`, hex-mangled `_0xNNNN` identifiers, cover names `MmgoCP`, `etDiOOB`). The payload's contents cannot be resolved without executing its decoder, embedded strings include hostname-shaped tokens that only materialize at runtime, and its purpose has no relationship to the package's advertised OREST CLI functionality. Naming the payload `math_init.js` and shadowing it behind short cover variables (`V`, `E`, `mu`) in `setup.mjs` disguises the dropper as build-time initialization. `lib/orest-micro/commands/publish/ssoAuth.js` additionally combines `child_process` with hardcoded outbound POST/GET calls. The Bun binary itself comes from a legitimate pinned URL, but the code it runs on `npm install` is attacker-authored, obfuscated, and executed on the installer's host with the installer's privileges.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
